finding: Time-travel Restore fires immediately with no confirm, and it permanently discards every change made after the scrub point — the board wires a confirm that the code never shows.
evidence: Board edge 163:113 -> 163:167 (History · Saves · restore-confirm) is 163:113's only outgoing reaction. Code: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:359-365 'Restore this point' -> handleRestore (:262-266) -> HistoryTab.tsx:195-201 composer.history.restoreEntry(entryId) with no confirm; HistoryTab.tsx:312-314 the panel band's 'Restore this version' does the same. HistoryManager.ts:721 clears redoStack and :724 truncates undoStack to slice(0, entry.index+1), then pushes a 'Restored to:' checkpoint — the work after the scrub point exists in no version and cannot be undone. Unlike the Saves-list restore, nothing calls versions.restoreVersion, so the safety snapshot at VersionTimelineManager.ts:289-299 never runs.
fix: Route both time-travel restore doors through a confirm before calling restoreEntry, and word it for THIS guarantee — restoreEntry saves nothing, so 163:167's 'your current work is saved as v4 first' is false here. Either take a safety version first (mirror VersionTimelineManager.ts:291) so 163:167's copy becomes true, or draw a distinct confirm that names what is discarded.

finding: While the time-travel drawer is open, a bare Enter keypress anywhere on the document restores the scrub point and truncates the undo stack.
evidence: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:269-286 registers a document-level keydown listener; :275-277 `e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey && !e.ctrlKey` -> handleRestore() -> restoreEntry (HistoryManager.ts:724). No board draws a keyboard contract for this; 163:113 shows only Exit and Restore buttons.
fix: Drop the bare-Enter binding, or make it open the confirm from W-H-01 rather than commit. A destructive, unconfirmed action on the most-pressed key in the app is the wrong default.

finding: In the All-changes list a row's timestamp is a button labelled 'Jump to 16:20' that silently rewrites history — same destructive restoreEntry, no confirm — and the board draws it as plain grey text.
evidence: ActivityView.tsx:529-541 renders the timestamp as a Button with aria-label/title `Jump to ${timeLabel}`; onClick -> handleTimestampClick (:360-393) -> composer.history.restoreEntry at :369, :375 and :384. HistoryManager.ts:721,724 clears redo and truncates undo. Board 163:2 draws the rows as 'Hero copy edited / Ali / 16:20' with no affordance and no reaction on any timestamp node.
fix: Same confirm as W-H-01, and relabel: 'Jump to' describes navigation, not discarding work. Draw the affordance on 163:2 so the control is visible before it is destructive.

finding: From the Published tab there is no way back to Saves — both tab labels are dead and the board itself carries no reaction, so a user who lands in the rollback list is stuck there.
evidence: Section reaction dump for 949:4474: only 949:4514 btn/rollback -> 184:2 plus three off-canvas hotspot/state frames (1720:17360/17364/17368). Node scan: 949:4474 itself = no reaction; 1657:7272 'Saves' = no reaction, no ancestor reaction; 1657:7274 'Published' = same. Contrast the shell-360 board, which wires its strip (963:4736 'Published tab' -> 949:4474, 963:4737 'Backups tab' -> 950:4474).
fix: Add a reaction on 1657:7272 -> 162:2, and on 1657:7274 keep it inert as the current tab. The panel boards must carry their own tab wiring, not inherit it from 963:4474.

finding: On the Saves board the 'Published' tab is not wired; the only reaction covering it is the whole-board fallback 162:2 -> 163:2, so clicking Published lands the user on History · Saves · changes while still believing they switched tabs.
evidence: 162:2 carries a frame-level ON_CLICK -> 163:2 (section reaction dump, row 1). Node scan of 162:2: 1656:7146 'Published' (rel 157,56) has no own reaction, reported only as ancestor-covered — that ancestor is the board-level edge. The one tab hotspot on the board is 876:6982 'hotspot/tab · History · Backups' -> 950:4474, i.e. the design-ahead Backups board, and there is no hotspot to 949:4474 anywhere on 162:2.
fix: Wire 1656:7146 -> 949:4474 and remove the frame-level 162:2 -> 163:2 fallback (it makes every node on the board a false hit). Given the two-tab data-safety risk, a tab that silently keeps you in Saves is worse than one that does nothing.

finding: The site menu's 'Publish history' entry opens the rollback version-picker modal directly, skipping the Published list — the user is put one Continue away from a redeploy without ever seeing what is live.
evidence: Inbound scan: 642:3401 'Site menu (⋯)' node 642:3673 'menu · Publish history' -> 184:2 (History · Published · roll-back confirm, which is in fact the picker — screenshot shows 'Roll back to a published version' with Cancel/Continue). Its sibling 642:3669 'menu · Version history' correctly -> 162:2. Code disagrees with the board: TabRouter.tsx:199-224 passes initialView='published' and HistoryTab.tsx:360-366 renders the PublishHistory LIST, not the picker.
fix: Repoint 642:3673 -> 949:4474. The picker is reached from the list's own 'Roll back to a published version…' button (949:4514).

finding: 'Restore a previous save' cannot be walked: the only per-row affordance drawn is a '⋯', no menu board exists anywhere for History, and the restore-confirm board is reachable only from an off-canvas prototype jump.
evidence: Rows on 162:2 carry only ⋯ glyphs (I241:1469;240:13, I241:1477;240:13, I241:1485;240:13, I241:1493;240:13) with no own reaction. Page-wide board-name search: Layers has 1082:4527 'Layers · context-menu', Pages has 1171:4713 'Pages · context-menu', Media has 1163:13695 — section 16 has none. 163:167 (restore-confirm) is entered only via 1671:7225 'hotspot/state · History · restore-confirm', an off-canvas 140x34 frame parked at rel y≈738. Code puts three buttons in that slot instead: VersionList.tsx:206-228 Compare / Restore / Delete.
fix: Either draw the History row ⋯ menu (Restore / Compare / Delete) and wire Restore -> 163:167, or redraw 162:2's rows with the inline actions the code actually renders. Today the board and the code disagree about the door AND the board's door leads nowhere.

finding: All 7 census candidates on this board are FINE — it is a component spec sheet, not a screen: three labelled state rows (SUGGESTED / EDITING / SAVING) at 680x402, and the board name names its source file.
evidence: Screenshot of 433:2348 shows section labels SUGGESTED / EDITING / SAVING. Candidates 433:2357/2359/2361 = the SUGGESTED row's Save/Edit/Dismiss (MilestoneSuggestionBanner.tsx:157-169), 433:2373 = the EDITING row's lone Save (:148-154), 433:2384/2386/2388 = the SAVING row's disabled Save + Edit + Dismiss (:160-162). Board's only reaction is 633:4021 hotspot/back -> 52:2.
fix: No change. Exclude spec-sheet boards from the census, or mark this one so it stops surfacing.

finding: Four '⋯' row menus on the Published list are DEAD — no reaction on the node, none on any ancestor, and no History context-menu board exists to open.
evidence: Node scan of 949:4474: 949:4491, 949:4497, 949:4503, 949:4509 (TEXT '⋯', 11x16 at rel x=253) all report NONE. The census missed them because it matches names and these are bare glyph nodes.
fix: The code's only per-row action is a 'Compare' text button (PublishHistory.tsx:312-322). Either redraw the row action as 'Compare' to match, or draw the ⋯ menu and wire it.

finding: Every control on the Saves board is mis-wired rather than dead: a frame-level catch-all sends any click — row menu, search field, Published tab, approval-band action — to the All-changes list, so an unwired control is indistinguishable from a wired one.
evidence: 162:2 carries a frame-level ON_CLICK -> 163:2 (section reaction dump, fetched 2026-09-05). Under the v2 census rule (a control counts as wired only when it or a real interactive ancestor has its OWN reaction, never the board), every control on 162:2 is unwired: the four row menus I241:1469/1477/1485/1493;240:13, the search box 1656:7154 'Search saves...', the 'Published' tab 1656:7146, and the approval band's action instance 229:1134. v2 does not list them because they are neither button-shaped containers nor imperative bare text — the ⋯ are single glyphs, the tab labels are nouns, and 229:1134's text child is literally named 'Button'. Same shape on 163:113 (I241:1501/1509/1517/1525;240:13).
fix: Remove the frame-level fallback on 162:2 and wire per-node. A whole-board catch-all makes an unwired control indistinguishable from a wired one in every audit that follows.

finding: The rolling-back progress caption draws a page count ('Publishing v5 as v7 · 18 of 27 pages') that nothing in the code can supply.
evidence: Board 184:37 screenshot. usePublishJob.ts:325 returns only `progress: status?.progress ?? 0`; PublishHistoryProps.rollbackJob is typed `{state, progress}` (PublishHistory.tsx:51, history/types.ts:41); the modal renders only 'Publishing v{target} as v{live+1}' (PublishHistory.tsx:426-429).
fix: Either surface pagesDone/pagesTotal from the publish job through rollbackJob, or drop the clause from the board. Half the caption is currently undeliverable.

finding: The version picker draws every row as selectable; the code has two unselectable kinds — the live version and a version whose snapshot was pruned — and neither disabled row is drawn.
evidence: PublishHistory.tsx:385 `const selectable = !isLive && r.rollbackable;` with :399 title 'This version''s snapshot is no longer stored'. Board 184:2 shows v6 with a 'live' chip but in normal weight, and v3/v4/v5 identical — no disabled treatment, and no pruned row at all. The 20-version retention rule that creates pruned rows is stated in the code header (PublishHistory.tsx:5-7) and in the empty-state copy (:260).
fix: Add a disabled row variant to 184:2 with the reason line, and show the live row as unselectable rather than merely chipped.

finding: The non-admin state of the rollback entry point is drawn nowhere — rollback is ADMIN-gated and degrades to a disabled button with an explanatory title.
evidence: PublishHistory.tsx:104 `const canRollback = roleAtLeast(useEditorRole(), 'ADMIN') !== false;` and :348-353 disable the button with title 'Ask an admin to roll back' (also disabled with 'There is only one published version' when rows.length < 2). Board 949:4474 draws only the enabled button 949:4514.
fix: Draw the disabled variant of 949:4514 with the reason, as a state of 949:4474.

finding: The banner's SAVING state is unreachable in the shipping code — `isLoading` is the AI-suggestion flag, and it is already false by the time the banner mounts.
evidence: useAutoMilestone.ts:161 setIsLoading(true), :189 setSuggestion(...), :198 setIsLoading(false) — both land in the same post-await continuation, so React batches them into one render with suggestion set and isLoading false. HistoryTab.tsx:345 renders the banner only when `milestoneSuggestion` is non-null, passing `isLoading={milestoneLoading}` (:348). MilestoneSuggestionBanner.tsx:160-162 `{isLoading ? '...' : 'Save'}` and `disabled={isLoading}` therefore never fire. The test proves nothing about the wiring — it passes the prop directly (MilestoneSuggestionBanner.test.tsx:65-67).
fix: Give the banner its own save-in-flight state around the `accept` call, and feed the SAVING row from that. Clicking Save currently shows no busy feedback at all.

finding: Accepting a milestone suggestion has no failure path — no catch, no toast, and no FAILED row on the board — while the sibling save path has all three.
evidence: useAutoMilestone.ts:272-280 `accept` awaits composer.versions.createVersion(versionName) bare; a rejection (storage quota, VersionTimelineManager.ts:159-177 write path) leaves the banner open and says nothing. Compare VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:178-188, which wraps the same call and pushes 'Save failed'. Board 433:2348 draws SUGGESTED / EDITING / SAVING and no error row.
fix: Wrap `accept` in try/catch with the same toast, and add a FAILED row to 433:2348.

finding: 'Name a milestone' has an entry point and no form — the '+ Save a version' link is drawn on 162:2 but the form it opens, and the one field the code requires, appear on no board in the file.
evidence: VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:431-472 renders the open form: a required 'Version name *' TextField, maxLength 50, a 0/50 counter (:449), Cancel and 'Save Version' with `disabled={!newVersionName.trim() || isSaving}` (:467) and an isSaving label swap (:469). The closed state — the link the board does draw — is :479-487. None of the 26 boards in section 16 is a save form (full board list read from section 1776:8374).
fix: Draw 'History · Saves · save-form' as a state of 162:2: the name field with its counter, the disabled-until-typed Save, and the saving state.

finding: Time-travel restore needs its OWN confirm — 163:167 cannot be reused, because its safety promise is false on that path.
evidence: 163:167 reads 'Your current work is saved as v4 first — nothing is lost.', which is true of versions.restoreVersion (VersionTimelineManager.ts:289-299 creates a safety version and aborts on failure). The time-travel path calls history.restoreEntry instead (HistoryTab.tsx:197), which creates no version and truncates the undo stack (HistoryManager.ts:724). The design-ahead Backups confirm already models the honest shape: 879:4518 says what is saved, what is replaced, and what is not affected.
fix: Draw 'History · Saves · time-travel · restore-confirm' naming what is discarded (every change after the scrub point) and whether anything is saved first, and wire 163:113 -> it -> 163:220.

finding: Deleting a saved version — a destructive action with its own inline confirm in code — has no board anywhere in the section.
evidence: VersionList.tsx:221-227 renders a per-row Delete; :192-203 swaps the row into a Delete/Cancel confirm; VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:224-234 runs it and toasts 'Deleted {name}'. Section 16's 26 boards contain restore-confirm, restoring, pruned-notice, load-error, loading and empty — no delete state. Board 162:2 draws neither the Delete action nor its confirm.
fix: Draw 'History · Saves · delete-confirm' as the row-level confirm the code renders, and add the Delete action to the row (or to the ⋯ menu of W-H-07).

finding: All three Published sub-state boards were drawn for the Publish panel, not the History panel: the header reads 'Publish' and the Saves/Published tab strip is absent — so in the state a user is most likely to be lost in, they cannot tell which tab they are in or get back to Saves.
evidence: Screenshots of 1704:8309 (empty), 1704:8256 (load-error) and 1704:8205 (loading) all show a 'Publish' panel header and no tab strip; their peers 162:2, 163:64, 453:4031 and 949:4474 all carry 'Version History' plus Saves/Published. In code these states render INSIDE HistoryTab, under its PanelFrame.Header title='Version History' (HistoryTab.tsx:215-221) and the view-switcher (:223-237): PublishHistory.tsx:243-263 returns the loading / error / empty EmptyStates from within that frame.
fix: Redraw the three with the History panel header and tab strip. This is the assignment's 'can the user tell which tab they are in' failing on three of the six Published boards.

finding: Three Saves boards still draw the retired two-tab 'Versions · Changes | Saves' chrome — no Published tab, no Milestones/All-changes chips, no search bar — contradicting the model the code and the sibling boards ship.
evidence: Screenshots: 163:2, 163:113 and 1138:4573 all title the panel 'Versions' and show a 'Changes | Saves' strip. The shipped model is HistoryView = 'saves' | 'published' with `changes` demoted to a filter chip (history/types.ts:9-28, HistoryTab.tsx:223-237 view-switcher then :242-271 filter chips), and the search bar renders for BOTH filters with placeholder 'Search changes...' (:43-46, :272-294). Their peers 162:2, 163:64, 163:167, 163:220, 163:269 and 453:4031 all draw the current chrome. The design-ahead Backups boards (950:4474, 1156:4620) also draw the retired strip, with 'Backups' overlapping 'Published'.
fix: Redraw 163:2, 163:113 and 1138:4573 on 162:2's chrome. Until then a designer reading 163:2 will rebuild a tab that was deliberately removed.

finding: Two Saves states the code produces have no board: the search-no-results state and the storage-unavailable state — and the latter also loses the '+ Save a version' action, so it is a dead end.
evidence: VersionList.tsx:362-378 branches on totalCount: 'No saved versions yet' vs 'No matching versions' / 'Try a different search term.' — 163:64 draws only the first. VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:327-342 returns a bare EmptyState when `!isAvailable` (VersionTimelineManager.ts:458-460, isStorageAvailable() && config.enabled); that early return sits above the main return, so the '+ Save a version' button at :479-487 never renders in it, unlike 163:64 which draws it.
fix: Draw 'History · Saves · no-search-results' and 'History · Saves · unavailable'. For the second, decide whether the save action should be present — the board says yes, the code says no.

finding: The two rollback modals are named backwards, and one of them borrows the word 'restore' from the Saves side — in a module where restoring a save and rolling back a deploy are different, differently-dangerous actions.
evidence: 184:2 is named 'History · Published · roll-back confirm' but its screenshot is the version PICKER ('Roll back to a published version', Cancel / Continue) — the code calls it exactly that (PublishHistory.tsx:361 'Board 184:2 — pick the version, THEN confirm it', Modal at :362-414). 184:24 is named 'History · Published · restore-confirm' but is the rollback confirm ('Roll back to v5?', ConfirmDialog at :506-541). The caption boards in section 24 already carry the right names: 186:7 'caption/Rollback · pick-version', 186:8 'caption/Rollback · confirm', 186:9 'caption/Rollback · publishing'.
fix: Rename 184:2 -> 'History · Published · rollback · pick-version' and 184:24 -> 'History · Published · rollback · confirm'. Reserve 'restore' for the Saves flow.

finding: The time-travel band's primary action is clipped on the board — the button reads 'this' with the rest of 'Restore this version' cut off by the 280px panel edge.
evidence: Screenshot of 163:113: the blue button at the band's right shows only 'this'. Node scan: 229:1140 (Button, 46x28 at rel x=218) with its label I229:1140;9:7 measured 42x90 — a label taller than its button, i.e. wrapped and overflowing. The code renders the same label in the same 280px band (HistoryTab.tsx:308-315, size='xs' with tw:h-7).
fix: Shorten to 'Restore' on the board and in HistoryTab.tsx:313 — the band already says which version is being previewed (:307).

finding: The rollback-failure modal draws only 'Try again'; the code also renders a 'Close' action beside it.
evidence: Screenshot of 453:4064 shows a single 'Try again' button (plus the ✕). PublishHistory.tsx:468-495 renders a ConfirmDialog with confirmLabel='Try again' AND cancelLabel='Close'.
fix: Add Close to 453:4064, or drop cancelLabel and rely on the ✕. A user who does not want to retry should not have to find the corner.

finding: 'Compare two versions' — one of this module's five jobs — has no board on either side: the Saves list's inline compare panel and the Published list's page-by-page diff are both fully built and drawn nowhere.
evidence: Saves: VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:415-428 mounts CompareView below an expanded row; CompareView.tsx:1-18 describes what it renders (visual/semantic toggle, screenshot diptych, change-count badges, AI summary button with result and error states). Entry is the per-row Compare at VersionList.tsx:206-213. Published: PublishHistory.tsx:291-292 mounts PublishDiffView in place of the whole list, entered from the per-row Compare at :312-322; PublishDiffView.tsx:1-13 renders page-level added/removed/changed badges plus its own SkeletonBlock loading and a back button. Section 16's 26 boards contain neither; section 17's Compare family is the approved-snapshot comparison, whose only code mount is ReviewTab (see W-N-04).
fix: Draw 'History · Saves · row-expanded (compare)' as a state of 162:2 and 'History · Published · diff' as a state of 949:4474. Both are finished surfaces with no picture, which is how they stay invisible to every design pass.

finding: A user cannot actually compare two versions of their choosing — both compare paths hardcode one side, so the job as stated is impossible in either tab.
evidence: Saves: VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:249-255 — `const latest = versions[0]; if (latest && latest.id !== versionId) { compareVersions(latest.id, versionId) }`. The left side is always the newest version, and expanding the newest row itself produces no comparison at all (the guard skips it, so CompareView renders with compareResult null at :419). Published: PublishHistory.tsx:317 pins `from` to `rows[i+1]` and `to` to `rows[i]`, i.e. adjacent pairs only — v6 against v3 cannot be asked for. No board draws a two-version picker.
fix: Either add a second-version selector to the compare entry (the rollback picker at 184:2 is the shape to copy), or retitle the affordance to what it does — 'Compare with current' on Saves, 'What changed since v{n-1}' on Published.

finding: Confirmed from the History side: the Saves approval band's 'Compare with current' is a real door into the Compare family, and it is one-way — deferring to W-N-01 / W-N-02 / W-N-03 rather than filing a third copy.
evidence: Board: 162:2 node 633:4005 'hotspot/state · Compare · side-by-side' ON_CLICK -> 168:2 (section 1776:8382 '17 · Compare · 16'), fetched 2026-09-05. Code: SavesChrome.tsx:129-138 renders 'Compare with current' and emits UI_PANEL_OPEN {panel:'review', screen:'compare'}, gated on isApproved (:83, :109). The band is drawn on 162:2, 163:2, 163:113, 163:220 and 163:269. W-N-03 establishes that Compare's four back chips all target 156:2 'Review panel · open' and that leaving Compare is setCompareOpen(false) (ReviewTab.tsx:501), so the History tab the user left is gone.
fix: No separate fix. When W-N-02's back chip is added to 168:2, 162:2 must be one of its opener-dependent destinations — this is the History-side confirmation that a Saves opener exists and is not hypothetical.

finding: The board's recent refit brought the rollback button and the four ⋯ glyphs back inside the 280px panel, but none of them was wired in the process — the ⋯ are still dead and the tab strip is still dead.
evidence: Fetched 2026-09-05, after the refit: 949:4514 btn/rollback measures 248x40 at rel (16,728) and is the board's only wired control (-> 184:2); 949:4491/4497/4503/4509 ('⋯', 11x16 at rel x=253) each report no reaction and no interactive ancestor; 1657:7272 'Saves' and 1657:7274 'Published' likewise; the frame 949:4474 itself carries no reaction. Screenshot confirms everything now sits inside the board.
fix: Wire in the same pass as W-H-04 and W-H-09. A geometry fix that leaves the wiring untouched moves a dead control from invisible to visible.
